#1305. Epileptic seizures nearly vanish after people receive experimental gene therapy in their brains

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mariana Lenharo is a reporter for Nature in New York City.

A scan shows the brain of a man with epilepsy. A newly developed gene therapy targets locations in the brain that are the root of epileptic seizures. Credit: Allison Robbert/The Washington Post/Getty

Three people with epilepsy resistant to drug treatment saw the number of seizures they had per month fall by more than 90% after gene-laden viruses were infused directly into their brains as part of an early-stage clinical trial1.

In each participant, the gene therapy was precisely targeted to a small patch of brain tissue that was the source of their seizures. The viruses carried a gene that makes neurons sensitive to a specific drug, which works like a dimmer switch for the therapy. By combining gene therapy with a drug — an approach known as chemogenetics — researchers can adjust a treatment’s potency, which is not possible with other types of gene therapy. The trial participants did not experience serious side effects.

Genetic therapies offer new hope against incurable brain diseases

Genetic therapies offer new hope against incurable brain diseases

The results were reported today in The New England Journal of Medicine by Yang Dai, a neurosurgeon at Xuanwu Hospital of Capital Medical University in Beijing, and his colleagues. “It’s exciting that there’s such a dramatic effect, and that they see very few side effects,” says Matthew Walker, a neurologist at University College London, who was not associated with the study.

But Walker cautions that the study is small. He is also concerned about the long-term use of the drug that participants took after receiving the gene therapy. High doses of the drug, an anti-psychotic called clozapine, have been associated with cardiovascular problems and other negative effects. “In the future, hopefully there are going to be better drugs” for this form of treatment, says Walker, who is the co-founder of the start-up company Focalis Bio in Canterbury, UK, which is also developing gene therapies for epilepsy.

The three trial participants were adults with a common form of epilepsy caused by hippocampal sclerosis, a type of scarring in a region of the brain called the hippocampus. The participants had this scarring on only one side of the hippocampus. All three had been diagnosed with epilepsy 10–25 years earlier and had developed resistance to at least two anti-seizure drugs. They also had at least two seizure episodes per month, on average, over the three months before they enrolled in the trial.

The experimental treatment uses a virus called adeno-associated virus 9 to deliver a gene to neurons in the affected area. The gene was engineered to produce proteins specifically in excitatory cells — the ones that are involved in seizures.

Brain editing now ‘closer to reality’: the gene-altering tools tackling deadly disorders

Brain editing now ‘closer to reality’: the gene-altering tools tackling deadly disorders

The gene instructs neurons to produce a receptor that binds to clozapine. Clozapine acts like a switch and activates these receptors, reducing the activity of the targeted neurons, the authors say. That reduced activity helps to suppress the abnormal electrical activity that triggers seizures.

Two weeks after receiving the gene therapy during surgery, participants began taking a low dose of clozapine every eight hours. Around two months later, the average number of seizures per month had dropped from 4.5 to 0.5 for two of the participants and from 4 to 0 for the third. Because the study design focused on safety, rather than measuring efficacy, there was no control group.

Walker says that there might be other explanations for the improvement. He adds that it is also not clear whether the effect was because of the combination of gene therapy and clozapine or from one of those components alone.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03566-2

Dai, Y. et al. N. Engl. J. Med. 395, 1867–1869 (2026).

#1304. Forget Barcola: Liverpool's Biggest Problem Was Made Clear in Palace Win

Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola have faced scrutiny for recent performances, but both players ultimately stepped up for Liverpool on Sunday afternoon at Selhurst Park.

The Reds strolled to a 3-1 victory in South London, courtesy of goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Wirtz and Alexander Isak, cancelling out Eddie Nketiah's late consolation. Andoni Iraola's men were fluid and dynamic in attack, while they relied on some Alisson Becker heroics to prevent them from conceding multiple first-half goals.

The result sees the Merseysiders move above Chelsea and into the Premier League's top four, rounding off a promising few weeks for Iraola ahead of the international break.

Liverpool invested heavily in Wirtz last summer, and again in Barcola this summer. Both players' performances are subsequently under a microscope, and understandably so.

However, few can have genuine complaints about either player's contributions against Palace. The pair combined for Wirtz's goal, before the German showed composure to lay the ball off to Isak inside the Eagles' box for the Swede's strike.

Wirtz and Barcola's Statistics vs Crystal Palace

Both players were bright and showed moments of quality that impacted the match. They'll rightfully be out of the firing line for the time being, although the victory shouldn't prevent Liverpool supporters from shining the spotlight on another player, who certainly didn't do himself justice against Palace, and generally hasn't this season.

Alongside Wirtz and Barcola, Cody Gakpo was deployed in Liverpool's trio behind Alexander Isak against Palace.

On paper, this is the strongest front four available to Iraola, but unlike the other three, Gakpo did very little to justify his inclusion. The likes of Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha were introduced late on, and both were able to showcase their attributes much more than the former PSV Eindhoven star was.

The bizarre nature of Liverpool's squad-building has seen them end up without a natural right-sided forward, so Gakpo has, perhaps unfairly, been shunted out to this side. However, this ploy was so ineffective in the first half at Selhurst Park on Sunday, that Iraola swapped his two wingers at the interval.

This did little to improve Gakpo's performance. In the opening 45 minutes, he was struggling when receiving the ball on the right, with the angles that playing on this side created not conducive to him being able to carry out dangerous attacking actions. In the second half, playing on the left solved this issue, but he still wasn't able to make much of the moments when he found himself driving inside onto his stronger foot.

The Netherlands international was ponderous and inefficient with his final action, and this resulted in an incredibly profligate display on the numbers.

He created just one chance, took no shots and accumulated just 0.05 expected assists. He also only beat his man once, whilst winning four of his eleven ground and aerial duels.

This was a completely non-existent showing from Gakpo, who is typically busy and industrious, even if not always polished in the final third.

Unfortunately for the player, this is a bit of a recurring theme this season. He's failed to contribute to a goal in each of his last five Premier League appearances, letting his minutes pass him by without impacting the game.

Liverpool have identified the perfect Van Dijk replacement, and they're ready to pay up to £90m to bring him in.

While Barcola and Wirtz continue to face the brunt of the Liverpool censure when things don't go well, and understandably so given the fees the Reds outlaid for the duo, Gakpo's quiet performances are going under the radar.

Iraola needs to start considering handing more minutes to his promising young wingers, Ngumoha and Munoz, instead of the 27-year-old.

#1302. Premier League legend David Silva, 40, makes emphatic return to football with man-of-the-match performance - three and a half years after retiring

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:23 EDT, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 10:15 EDT, 8 November 2026

David Silva made his mark in his first game since coming out of retirement after scoring on debut in a man-of-the-match display for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin on Saturday.

Last month, the Manchester City icon revealed he was lacing his football boots in a professional sense again for the first time since 2023.

The 40-year-old started for Sha Tin and broke the deadlock against HK Rangers from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Silva stepped up and coolly passed the ball into the bottom left-hand corner - sending Hong Kong Rangers goalkeeper Ka-Yu Yip the wrong way.

The playmaker's goal sparked mass celebrations from his team-mates and the fans in the stands - with many taking their phones out of their pockets to record the moment.

However, Silva's debut didn't go as smoothly as planned as the visitors equalised in the 65th minute through Ibrahim Yakubu Nassam.

Some Spanish guy just scored a penalty for Sha Tin#DavidSilva #hkpl #hkfootball pic.twitter.com/JCbiYZEKE0

David Silva scored for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin with this penalty in their 1-1 draw on Saturday

The 40-year-old celebrates with his team-mates after scoring against Hong Kong Rangers

Silva was named man-of-the-match, in what his first competitve match in over three years

With 11 minutes remaining, Silva was then booked before he was substituted in the 84th minute with his side down to 10 men following Maxwell Ansah's 81st-minute red card for a second bookable offence.

Despite failing to take all three points, Silva did collect the man-of-the-match award after the full-time whistle.

Sha Tin currently sit 10th in the Hong Kong Premier League with five points from their opening seven matches. They sit one point and place above bottom-placed Eastern AA, who occupy the sole relegation spot, and 14 points adrift of table-toppers North District.

Silva called it a day on his playing career back in 2023 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament while playing for Real Sociedad.

He is most famed for spending ten years at Manchester City between 2010 and 2020, where he won 11 major honours; four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups. Much of that time period, though, is now under scrutiny.

He also has a statue outside the Etihad Stadium, and won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, as well as Euro 2008 and Euro 2012.

Upon joining Sha Tin, ex-Valencia midfielder Silva said in an Instagram video: 'I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong.'

Silva will hope to lead his side to victory when they take on Southern District in the Hong Kong League Cup Losers play-offs on Saturday.

Manchester United will spend the entire international break in the relegation zone after drawing 4-4 at home to Aston Villa on Sunday afternoon.

First, Alysson swept the ball underneath Senne Lammens after John McGinn had found the Brazilian in space in the box. Then, Lammens spilt the first goalscorer's effort into the path of Nicolas Jackson, who tapped home from close range.

However, the equaliser did come moments later on the stroke of half-time when Noussair Marzaoui's cutback found Tielemans, who powered beyond a hapless Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery's team started the second half just as they did the first, on the front foot and hungry for a lead. They were awarded a spot kick two minutes after the interval when Diogo Dalot tripped Alysson inside United's box. John McGinn made no mistake with the ensuing penalty, emphatically smashing the ball past Lammens to re-establish Villa's advantage.

The mountain got bigger for United to climb five minutes later as Leon Goretzka tapped in on the goal line following a bizarre backwards header from Yoro. This goal looked to have killed the game, which faded into a lull in the final half an hour as Villa attempted to preserve their lead.

After a rough opening 15 minutes for the Englishman, in which he looked visibly ruffled by Villa's brazen start, he settled into the game. Sweeping up well several times, he guided a rocked Yoro through the rest of the first half before he was forced off at the break with an injury.

The Portuguese has faced constant criticism this season, lambasted for his defensive deficiencies and his wastefulness in the final third. He did little to silence the critics in this game.

The United academy graduate was surprisingly astute defensively, snapping into tackles to prevent Villa from running at his team's vulnerable backline.

Whilst United were threatening for much of the game, Bryan Mbeumo was unusually quiet, particularly in the first half.

#1300. Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he said. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

“It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

#1299. Amorim: ‘Milan cannot have day off, losing must feel like end of the world’

Ruben Amorim explains the kind of ‘mentality’ he wants to always see from inconsistent Milan after their win in Genoa. ‘There is no day off. It’s feeling that losing is the end of the world.’

The Rossoneri remain completely unpredictable, as they have lurched from negative to positive results and back again, repeating the pattern at Marassi.

After the midweek round defeat to Bologna, victory over Inter in the Derby della Madonnina and 2-0 Europa League loss to Ferencvaros on Thursday, they again flipped for a 2-1 win away to Genoa.

Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scored the early goals, hanging on under pressure following the Mikkel Ellertsson deflected strike, to end Genoa’s impressive run of three consecutive victories.

“I am proud again with my players, I said before the game the most important thing was to be competitive, because if we have this attitude in every game, we are closer to winning every game,” Amorim told DAZN Italia.

“There are moments when we change the game, we go for the second ball and play different types of football, that is the sign of a great team, who can play different ways during the same match.”

The problem therefore is managing to keep that going more consistently than just once per week, but meanwhile they are in fourth place and only five points off leaders Lazio.

“We can win any game, but I cannot tell you we are going to reach this at the end of the season, as I cannot feel the consistency is there yet. I don’t want to say anything more than we are able to win the next game, but then it depends on a lot of things,” added Amorim.

“If we have all the players available, we will be better not just in Serie A, but also in Europe. This cycle of games was hard for us because of everything that happened, but I can say that if we are competitive, we can win any game in the league.

“So let’s focus on that and go day by day.”

Now Milan go into the break for international duty and hope the injury crisis can calm a little, as they were already missing Strahinja Pavlovic, Fikayo Tomori, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Pietro Terracciano and Alexis Saelemaekers.

The coach had said that Milan were “not ready to be competitive every three days,” and it does seem as if they reserve all their determination, passion and energy for the weekends. What does he mean by competitive?

“It’s about the mentality. When you play for Milan, there is no day off. You cannot switch off on Thursday the way we did and then switch back on come Sunday. That is not possible. It’s not going to work,” insisted the coach.

“It’s not physical, it’s about having that panic of losing. That does not mean being afraid of losing, it’s feeling that losing is the end of the world. That is the feeling I want in my team, so it depends on that.”

Goncalo Ramos was again involved in the build-up to both goals, but does not contribute actual goals or assists.

“It’s hard for a striker when he doesn’t score a goal, but we don’t spend a lot of time in the final third. We have a lot of possession, but when we reach the final third more often, Goncalo Ramos is going to score many goals. It is a team problem, the way we play is not helping Ramos, whereas he is helping the team.

“It is a process, we need to have Ramos spending 60 per cent of his time in the opponent’s box, and we are not there yet,” concluded Amorim.

#1298. Ex-Premier League Referee Condemns 'Worst Mistake' In Arsenal Vs Hull

Former Premier League referee Graham Barber has admitted that the referee and the VAR made "probably the worst mistake anybody could make" during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Hull City at the weekend.

The Gunners continued their fine form and opened up a five-point lead at the top of the Premier League table with a hard-fought 1-0 win over the Tigers at the Emirates Stadium.

The win came as a result of Martin Odegaard's 72nd minute strike, but things could have been made a lot easier had they been awarded a first half penalty.

Kai Havertz went down in the box after having his shirt pulled by Hull star Nobel Mendy, with referee FaraiHallam waving away appeals for a spot-kick. However, the referee was asked to review the incident on the pitchside monitor by the VAR, although it was determined that Havertz was in an offside position before he had his shirt pulled.

Hallam explained his decision to the crowd, saying it was a foul, but that the offside rule negated the need for a penalty. That is not true when it comes to the laws of the game, however, with a clear mistake made by the on-pitch referee and the VAR in not awarding a spot-kick.

Speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, Barber explained the laws of the game and said it was the "worst mistake" a referee could make.

He said: "Thankfully, it didn't affect the result of the match and there would have been some implications, I think if it had affected the result of the match, because I think the best thing for me here, is to read the laws of the game, or the excerpt from Law 11, which is the offside.

And the law reads, 'if a player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball, and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence'.

"So, let's look at that incident. The incident is really quite clear, it's a clear foul, it's a clear pulling of the shirt, he was clearly attempting to go and play the ball, and the sad thing is, they got this wrong.

"Both VAR and the referee got this wrong, and the point about this is they got this wrong in law.

"Week in, week out we have discussions about opinions and you may think one thing, I may think another thing, fans may think another thing, the opposing fans may think something else, because the game's all about opinions.

"What we do want to avoid though is decisions being made that are incorrect in law. And in this particular case, Arsenal should clearly have had a penalty kick. Kai Havertz was fouled in an attempt to play the ball, and that should have superseded the offside decision, so it should have been a penalty kick.

"The referees are the custodians of the laws of the game and as custodians of the law, they need to implement the laws and if a law is not implemented, that's probably the worst mistake anybody could make.

"I can make a decision based on opinion, you can make a decision based on opinion, but at the end of the day, there's no opinion when it comes to law."

Kai Havertz was pulled to the ground in the box.

#1297. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. “We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1296. Cutting-edge technique uncovers how the spine’s shock absorbers bear load

Hanna Isaksson is in the Department of Biomedical Engineering, Lund University, 22363 Lund, Sweden.

By combining information from two X-ray techniques, it is possible to visualize the response of soft biological tissue to mechanical loads on multiple scales, as Newham et al.1 write in Nature. The authors use this method to observe how compressive loads are transmitted between micrometre- and nanometre-scale components of intervertebral discs — the shock-absorbing structures found between the vertebrae of the spine. The information provided by such studies could help scientists to design synthetic materials that mimic the remarkable properties of biological tissues.

#1295. Aston Villa Director Calls Out Roy Keane’s Man Utd Equaliser Verdict

Aston Villa director of football operations Damian Vidagany has slammed Roy Keane's assessment of Patrick Dorgu's equaliser being allowed to stand in a 4-4 draw against Manchester United.

Unai Emery's side were heading towards all three points when second half stoppage time arrived but Joshua Zirkzee's 90+2nd minute strike gave United hope. They capitalised with a late corner with Zion Suzuki missing the ball and Dorgu heading home, much to Emery's frustration.

The Villa boss seemed to take issue with the manner of the goal when he stormed down the tunnel after watching the ball find the net. There are question marks over United goalkeeper Senne Lammens potentially obstructing Suzuki when the Japanese shot-stopper attempted to claim the ball in midair.

Emery has since explained that his actions were a response to spurning a victory in the dying embers rather than the goal itself. Vidagany has vented his frustrations with Dorgu's header along with Roy Keane's analysis after the match.

Keane spoke on Sky Sports about Lammens' possible involvement in the goal and whether he felt the Belgian had leaned into Suzuki. VAR had checked and cleared this and the former United captain agreed with this verdict: "Football is a contact sport. I have no problem with it."

Vidagany wasn't happy with Keane’s narrative of “contact sport” and posted his thoughts on X:

To put in context this convenient narrative of “ contact sport” we’ve been told by Referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six hard box was not going to be allowed anymore. Lammens not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion. Having said that we played good Match and we must do better than last 6 minutes. We will do and we will improve. But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.

Lammens doesn't fully make contact with Suzuki but rather puts his back to the goalkeeper, who fails to collect the ball. Former Villa winger Ashley Young agreed with Keane and said that he didn't feel there was enough in it.

Emery did suggest in his post-match interview that Villa would have been awarded a foul for Lammens' actions in other leagues. He said that this was an 'adaption' to the Premier League for Suzuki to deal with players 'pushing and disturbing' him.

The Premier League operates under IFAB rules and the guidelines regarding impending a goalkeeper make for interesting reading. It states that if an attacker moves into the path of a goalkeeper to block their line of movement without attempting to play the ball, it is an offence.

Impeding with contact includes body checks, pushing or backing into the keeper and in this case it could be determined that Lammens is guilty of the latter offence. The rule also determines impeding without contact to be directly stepping into their path to force them to stop or alter direction.

The Villa boss lost his head after throwing away a win.

Referees also strictly enforce protection of goalkeepers jumping to catch or punch the ball. This is why Vidagany's dismissive response to Keane claiming football is a contact sport holds merit.

#1294. Serie A line-ups: Fiorentina vs. Juventus

Nick Woltemade is declared fit to start in attack for Juventus against Fiorentina in Serie A on Sunday evening, as Paolo Vanoli makes just one alteration to his winning side.

You can follow the action as it unfolds on the Football Italia Liveblog.

Hosts Fiorentina find themselves in 15th place in the Serie A standings ahead of kick-off. They have won two, drawn two and lost six of their opening 10 league games this season, but are unbeaten across their last two, claiming a 4-2 victory over Sassuolo last weekend.

Juventus are in seventh place after the first 10 league games of the season after five wins, two draws and three defeats at the start of the Serie A season. They picked up a much-needed 2-0 victory over Napoli last time out in the league and have since beaten AZ Alkmaar 2-1 away from home in the Europa League.

The Bianconeri still have a hefty injury list that includes Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Manuel Locatelli, Nico Gonzalez and Francisco Conceicao.

Nick Woltemade is declared fit despite struggling with a bout of flu, and is included in Sunday’s starting line-up alongside Randal Kolo Muani in attack. Jeremie Boga completes the attacking trident.

Paolo Vanoli has made just one change to his side that defeated Sassuolo last weekend: Pedro Goncalves is introduced in midfield in place of Marco Brescianini.

Kick-off is due at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

Fiorentina (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Jiménez, Dragusin, Viery, Joao Mario; Ndour, Oulai; Mastantuono, Gonçalves, Njie; Pellegrino.

Juventus (4-3-3): Vicario; Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumí, Cabal; McKennie, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners; Kolo Muani, Woltemade, Boga.

#1293. Crystal Palace To Sack Pierre Sage

Crystal Palace have decided to sack manager Pierre Sage following their 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, as per The Athletic. GIVEMESPORT also understands chairman Steve Parish is planning to let the Frenchman go.

Sage was only appointed as Eagles boss over the summer, replacing Oliver Glasner, who left for Nottingham Forest following a successful two-and-a-half year stint in South London. The French coach was sounded out by the Selhurst Park hierarchy after leading Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season.

Despite these impressive credentials, Sage hasn't been able to elicit strong performances from his players at Palace, who currently sit bottom of the Premier League after 10 matches.

The Conference League champions have won just two league matches under their new boss, and Parish has subsequently opted to part ways with the 47-year-old manager.

Lasting until November, just 16 games, Sage will only narrowly surpass Frank de Boer as the shortest-serving manager in Palace's recent history.

The Dutchman famously lasted just four matches at the start of the 2017/18 season, after failing to pick up a single point during his short-lived tenure in the Selhurst Park dugout.

The final straw for Sage was seemingly Palace's dire defeat against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. Palace will now search for a successor in the upcoming international break, as they desperately look for a coach who can take them away from a relegation battle, whilst coping with the demands of Europa League football.

GIVEMESPORT understands both Thomas Frank and Sean Dyche are among the contenders, as are Tony Popovic and Vitor Pereira.

Frank is seen as an early contender for the job, having been interviewed in the summer. Parish also has admiration for free agent Dyche and Coventry boss Frank Lampard. Another option is former Palace defender and current Australian national team boss Popovic but his lack of Premier League pedigree could count against him.

Pereira, who worked with Palace sporting director at Wolves, is also available and hoping for another Premier League job after leaving Nottingham Forest over the summer.

The following are said to be the current frontrunners to commence a new era at Selhurst Park:

Dyche is available after being sacked by Nottingham Forest mid-way through last season. Meanwhile, Frank has been out of a job since his disastrous stint at Tottenham last term.

Robbie Keane would represent a more left-field choice, although the Irish legend is said to have impressed in his most recent role as head coach of Hungarian side Ferencvaros.

There have been calls for Eddie Howe to replace Sage, although the former Newcastle boss is reportedly in line to succeed Michael Carrick at Manchester United, if and when the Red Devils manager is dismissed.

Meanwhile, former Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna is said to be in the running. The Northern Irishman has been out of a job since stepping down from his role at Portman Road at the end of last season, having led the Tractor Boys to another promotion.

Palace boss Sage is under growing pressure after a crushing derby defeat

#1292. Inside the insane trophy room of Chelsea legend Branislav Ivanovic: Framed pictures of his 42 goals, a ring from Didier Drogba... and an LED football pitch

Published: 04:50 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EDT, 8 November 2026

Legendary Chelsea defender Branislav Ivanovic's insane private trophy room has gone viral after a fan posted a tour of the museum online.

The now 42-year-old made 377 appearances for the Blues during a nine-year stint at the club from 2008 to 2017.

He enjoyed a hugely successful time with the west London side, winning ten trophies and becoming one of the club's most decorated defenders.

As well as winning three Premier League titles he landed three FA Cups,  the League Cup, the Community Shield and the Europa League. He also has a Champions League winners' medal with the Blues, though the Serb did miss out on playing in the 2012 final after famously being told by Geoff Shreeves live on Sky Sports that he was suspended following their win over Barcelona in the semi-final.

Branislav Ivanovic won 10 trophies with Chelsea across nine years with the Blues

The Chelsea legend has built a private trophy room in his hometown of Sremska Mitrovica to rival any other

In a video posted to Instagram a fan from Ivanovic's hometown Sremska Mitrovica explained he was allowed access to the private showroom and documented the breadth of trophies, personal honours and shirts he has collected throughout his illustrious career.

Many of the souvenirs are from his time in Russia with Lokomotiv Moscow and Zenit St Petersburg, as well as those he got at Chelsea.

The private museum holds over hundreds of shirts alone and has an entire wall adorned with shirts just given to him and signed by someone he either played with or played against including the likes of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Neymar and Javier Zanetti.

Most Chelsea fans will remember Ivanovic's most crucial goals such as his winners in the Champions League round of 16 against Napoli and the 2013 Europa League final against Benfica.

And the Serbian appears to have made an effort to immortalise every single one of his club goals by framing and displaying a photo of all 42 from throughout his career.

Amongst other quirky designs, the room has a set of football leg stools for guests to sit on at the bar

Mourinho gets a mention having won the Premier League, Fa Cup and League cup with the Serbian in the 2014-15 season

There is also a replica of every trophy he has won in his career as well and a specialty ring he received as a gift from Didier Drogba after Chelsea's 2012 Champions League triumph.

Ivanovic didn't forget to add some style to the room by installing an LED football pitch to light the room and putting swanky football leg chairs at a fully stocked bar.

He even has a slide solely dedicated to displaying quotes from his former manager Jose Mourinho including the Special One's description of Ivanovic as 'The Perfect One'.

Since leaving Chelsea in 2017 the Serb moved back to Zenit St Petersburg before ending his career back in England with West Brom in 2021.

#1291. Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a big moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”

Forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to quickly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner said: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

“It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”

We knew the margins would be really small. They are extremely well coached and organised. The longer the game goes on they gain more belief. We had to be so patient - and clinical when we got the chance. The way they were defending, they were more comfortable. We have another three big chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating them, they will come.

When you see their goal it’s deflected otherwise, it’s straight to the gloves of Matz Sels. You have periods in football where you feel everything going against you and then there are periods when things are on your side.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good.

Noni [Madueke], Jurrien [Timber], Mikel [Merino] was brilliant when he came on and Viktor [Gyokeres] really changed the game - all of them did and that’s what we need. Noni obviously the highlight because he scored the goal and that’s the difference.

Sometimes you can get frustrated with teams who are difficult to break down. First half we didn’t have a shot on target and that’s something we discussed. We had another two big ones in the second half but the only one on target we had was a little deflection and it’s in.

Great reaction [after scoring goal], to have the will to defend a really open and difficult and stressful situation.

We knew it would be a tough game, it always is against Arsenal. They have a good team. But we feel we can change the result, maybe a draw, maybe a win. Now we have to put it in the past and focus on the next match.

We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas. We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best.

If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd so we know that we’re going to start some and finish some and for me it’s the same mentality every time I just want to create or score.

Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.

We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

#1290. He Played For Arsenal at 19, Then He Was Sent to Prison For 4 Years

15 years after making his Arsenal debut at the age of 19, Jay Emmanuel-Thomas was sentenced to four years in prison.

Born in East London, Emmanuel-Thomas joined the Gunners' academy at the age of eight. He steadily progressed through the various youth ranks before going on to make five appearances for the first team under Arsene Wenger.

After a series of uninspiring loan spells, Arsenal parted ways with the striker, selling him to Ipswich Town for an undisclosed fee. He'd go on to enjoy stints at Queens Park Rangers, MK Dons and Gillingham, before spending time in Scotland, Thailand and India.

However, his career at the professional level was essentially brought to an end when he was arrested and charged with orchestrating the attempted importation of drugs in 2024.

An extremely prolific forward at youth level, big things were expected of Emmanuel-Thomas as he approached adulthood. He became the captain of Arsenal's under-18s when he was just 16, and signed his first professional contract in 2008, at the age of 17.

Wenger, who was known for blooding young talent at every opportunity, started to take note of Emmanuel-Thomas' exploits in the academy during the 2008/09 season. The Frenchman named the centre-forward in multiple matchday squads, although he kept him at arm's length from the pitch, prioritising the player's physical development instead of rushing him into senior football.

However, such was the level of Emmanuel-Thomas' performances in the reserves that he became irresistible to Wenger in the following campaign. In January 2010, the striker made his senior debut in an FA Cup tie against Stoke City. He started as Arsenal's centre-forward, but was substituted after 66 minutes.

Although this was Emmanuel-Thomas' only appearance that season for the Gunners' first team, as he was shipped out on loan to Blackpool and Doncaster Rovers at various points during the 2009/10 campaign, Wenger showered the youngster with praise at the time.

"Jay is knocking very hard on my door - with two hands," the legendary manager said.

"He has outstanding quality. He works very hard to get his fitness right. When his fitness is right, Jay will be not only a good player but a great player. One thing is for sure - he can score goals. That is a massive talent you cannot give to people, his right foot, left foot, he is unbelievable in front of goal."

Despite this effusive praise, Wenger's words didn't translate into his team selection the following season. Emmanuel-Thomas was granted just four opportunities to play for Arsenal in 2010/11, including cameos alongside the likes of Jack Wilshere and Cesc Fabregas, before again being shunted out temporarily to Cardiff City.

At the end of that season, the Gunners opted to cash in on their promising young striker, selling him to Ipswich in a move that hurt many supporters, who had believed the number nine could eventually succeed Robin van Persie at the Emirates.

A below-par stint in the Championship with the Tractor Boys saw Emmanuel-Thomas leave for League One Bristol City in the summer of 2013. Revitalising his career with the Robins, the Englishman enjoyed two productive years in Bristol in the third tier, before returning to the Championship with QPR.

However, a flat spell in West London proved to be the beginning of the end for Emmanuel-Thomas at the top level. Within four years of signing for the Hoops, he was in Thailand playing for PTT Rayong.

This was the start of his 'journeyman' era, which involved six clubs in six years, ending in the Scottish Championship with Greenock Morton. Then came the controversy.

The Gunners got this one massively wrong.

In September 2024, Emmanuel-Thomas was arrested and accused of being responsible for importing 60kg of cannabis, worth an estimated £600,000. This cannabis was unearthed in suitcases arriving at Stansted Airport from Bangkok, carried by the footballer's girlfriend, who had been duped into believing she was transporting gold.

In May 2025, the Hale End academy graduate pleaded guilty to smuggling drugs from Thailand at Chelmsford Crown Court. He was sentenced to four years in prison but was released on parole after spending just a month behind bars.

He has since started playing for Whitehawk, a semi-professional club in Brighton, in the 7th tier of English football.

#1289. 17-year-old Cassano impresses in front of Italy head coach Mancini

Riccardo Cassano made the most of his opportunity to impress in front of Italy national team head coach Roberto Mancini on Sunday, scoring the winning goal in a 3-2 victory for Como’s Primavera side against their counterparts from Fiorentina in the presence of the CT.

The 17-year-old Como talent was the most surprising inclusion of Mancini’s latest Italy squad, announced on Thursday, for November’s Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium.

Cassano has never previously appeared in a competitive senior fixture at club level, but will have an opportunity to impress with the senior Italy national team squad at Coverciano next week.

It has been confirmed by the FIGC that Cassano, along with 18-year-old Parma talent Simone Lontani will train with the senior squad for the first few days of the camp, before going off to play with the youth sides in order to gain realistic minutes this international break.

Cassano had an opportunity to show what he has to offer ahead of the start of the international break (on Monday), as Mancini went in-person to watch him play in the Primavera match between Como and Fiorentina at Viola Park on Sunday.

Fiorentina took an early two-goal lead, but Como turned the result on its head within 20 minutes in the second half, with Cassano scoring the winning goal for 3-2 from midfield.

#1288. He Was Teammates with Harry Kane and Luka Modric - Now He's Convicted of Fare Dodging

A former teammate of Harry Kane and Luka Modric has this week been convicted of fare dodging in London, with his career taking a very different turn from that of his two Ballon d’Or-winning counterparts.

The news comes in the same week that Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win football’s most prestigious individual award, following in the footsteps of Michael Owen, who claimed the famous Golden Ball in 2001.

Kane’s journey began in humble surroundings, with the striker turning out for the likes of Fleetwood Town before climbing the footballing ladder at Premier League side Tottenham and, later, Champions League contenders Bayern Munich.

That rollercoaster ride through the football pyramid has seen him share the pitch with all sorts of characters from different backgrounds. One former teammate has now been found guilty of a rather unexpected offence - dodging a £7 train fare, despite having played a sport where lucrative contracts are not rare.

According to the Wimbledon Guardian, Sebastien Bassong, now 41, was caught following a friend through the ticket barriers at St Paul’s Station on May 2.

A subsequent investigation by a Transport for London (TfL) officer revealed that Bassong had been using a train driver’s nominee pass that did not belong to him.

In a statement to the court, TfL revenue control officer Adebukola Anifowose said she spotted Bassong at 1.08pm “pretend to tap an Oystercard enclosed in a white wallet before tailgating through the wide-aisle gate behind another male”.

Bassong appeared at Wimbledon Magistrates’ Court on Friday, October 30, where he was convicted of travelling without a valid ticket. He was fined £220 and ordered to pay the £7 fare, £250 in prosecution costs and an £88 victim surcharge, bringing the total to £565.

The friend who accompanied him later told the TfL officer that he had given Bassong the pass because he was “experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment”.

Bassong's career never really took off after he left Tottenham following just three seasons in north London. His only notable success thereafter came at Norwich City, where he made 123 appearances, won the club's Player of the Year award in 2013, and helped the Canaries secure promotion from the Championship via the playoffs in 2015.

He then spent a season at Peterborough United but managed just one appearance in the EFL Trophy as he continued to struggle with a recurring knee injury.

The same problem prevented him from making any lasting impact at Volos, where he made three appearances in the Greek Super League during the 2019/20 season before announcing his retirement. Before that decision, during lockdown, he featured in a pre-season friendly for Isthmian League side Haringey Borough.

These days, Bassong works as a strategic performance and leadership advisor, motivational coach and public speaker. He has also taken part in charity boxing events, including one organised by Pro Project Promotions, where he knocked out former Arsenal defender Armand Traore.

#1287. Winning is the only thing that matters to Rangers midfielder Dan Neil as Ibrox club continue to gain momentum in title challenge

Published: 13:52 EDT, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EDT, 8 November 2026

Rangers midfielder Dan Neil admits he couldn’t care less about how his side go about picking up points as long as the wins keep coming.

The stand-in captain netted the crucial second in Saturday’s hard-fought victory over St Mirren in Paisley after Ryan Naderi had given the visitors a first-half lead from the penalty spot.

It was a result which extended Rangers’ unbeaten run to 12 in all competitions as they continue to build momentum following an unconvincing start to the campaign, and Neil insists that’s the only thing that matters at this stage.

He said: ‘I think every good team just finds a way to win.

‘Obviously, we’d like to win by four or five goals every single week but unfortunately that’s just not football. I do think it’s an area that we can improve on.

‘There’s been too many games this year where maybe we don’t get that second goal and it’s a bit nervy. Teams get a little bit of confidence off that and the momentum shifts.

Dan Neil savours the moment after putting the seal on Rangers' win with the second goal

‘I think it’s definitely something that we can improve on, putting teams to bed when we do go 1-0 up and go 1-0 up early doors when we’re creating chances.

‘But at the same time, finding a way to win is the most important way and whether that’s 1-0 or 5-0, at the end of the day it’s three points.’

While Rangers weren’t quite at their best in Paisley, they did more than enough to halt their poor recent run away from home.

Back-to-back 2-2 draws at Dundee and Hearts last month saw valuable points dropped in what is shaping up to be a tight title race, and Neil was delighted to get back to winning ways ahead of the international break.

‘The last two away results and performances really haven’t been us,’ said the former Sunderland man. ‘It was important that we didn’t have another one of them going into the break and have it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

‘Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. It’s important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you’ve seen that on Saturday night.

‘It was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us and make sure that we win the game. I think there was some good football played for the majority of the game and we also dug in when we had to. That’s credit to every single player in that dressing room.’

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.
